issue.title: [RFC pruning] Separate Driver mechanical batching from caller semantic guarded runs
issue.body:
## Goal

Resolve the boundary between trycua/cua#2794/#3494 batching and RFC caller-side guarded runs.

Pinned main: `c5ee191c02b11448ffefcc38b78b064a87d8ef23`.

Relevant:
- #5 guarded run
- #6 stale-target batch
- #43 abstraction pressure
- trycua/cua#2794
- trycua/cua#3494

## Candidate boundary

**Driver/mechanical batch**
- transport/dispatch efficiency;
- existing authorization per child;
- fail-fast;
- no semantic claim that child N remains valid after child N-1.

**Caller guarded run**
- decides whether another semantic action is still justified;
- reobserves/re-proves dependencies;
- evaluates postconditions;
- may choose a new fresh target.

## Experiment / review

Try to implement one workflow using the wrong owner in each direction:
- put semantic dependency logic into a Driver batch;
- emulate mechanical batching entirely in caller round trips.

Use the failure to sharpen the ownership boundary.

## Acceptance

Final RFC must not create a competing batch API if upstream #2794/#3494 owns mechanical composition.

## Deliverable

Two-column ownership contract and exact integration point between the two mechanisms.
